title: APOLLO: SGD-like Memory, AdamW-level Performance
problem: AdamW optimizer for LLM training maintains first and second moments, tripling memory requirements over model weights alone (28 GB optimizer states for LLaMA-7B). This forces smaller batch sizes, more GPUs, or lower-end models.
motivation: Existing memory-efficient optimizers either require expensive SVD (GaLore, Fira), suffer performance gaps (Flora), or still have significant overhead (Adam-mini). A memory-efficient optimizer matching AdamW performance without SVD is needed for scalable LLM training.
method: APOLLO identifies that AdamW's element-wise learning rate adaptation can be coarsened to channel-wise or tensor-wise scaling without performance loss. It approximates channel-wise gradient scaling factors using an auxiliary low-rank optimizer state in a random-projected space (not SVD). Algorithm: (1) project full gradient to low-rank space via random Gaussian matrix; (2) apply AdamW on the low-rank gradient to get low-rank moments; (3) extract channel-wise scaling factors from low-rank moments; (4) apply scaling to full gradient for weight update. APOLLO-Mini uses tensor-wise (rank-1) scaling for SGD-level memory. The random projection matrix is resampled every T=200 steps. A Norm-growth Limiter stabilizes training.
key_novelty: Theoretical proof (via Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma) that random projection preserves gradient scaling factors up to a bounded ratio, enabling SVD-free low-rank approximation that is rank-insensitive and achieves SGD-level memory at AdamW performance.
contributions: Channel-wise structured learning rate update sufficient for LLM training (replacing element-wise AdamW)
APOLLO: channel-wise gradient scaling via random-projected low-rank auxiliary optimizer state
APOLLO-Mini: tensor-wise scaling with rank-1 sub-space achieving SGD-level optimizer memory
Theoretical bound on scaling factor approximation error via JL lemma
SVD-free operation: random projection reduces SVD cost (10 min per update for 7B) to negligible
3x training throughput on 8xA100-80GB via 4x larger batch sizes
First pre-training of LLaMA-13B with naive DDP on A100-80GB
First LLaMA-7B pre-training on a single GPU under 12 GB (with INT8 quantization)
workloads: LLaMA pre-training (60M to 7B) on C4 dataset
Fine-tuning on commonsense reasoning (LLaMA-3.2-1B, LLaMA-3-8B, Gemma-7B, Mistral-7B)

metrics.perplexity_vs_adamw_llama1b: APOLLO-Mini achieves lower perplexity than AdamW at 2.60G vs 7.80G optimizer memory
metrics.throughput_improvement: ~3x on LLaMA-7B (8xA100) via 4x larger batch sizes
metrics.perplexity_improvement_vs_galore: Up to 3.62 points better at same memory budget

limitations: Norm-growth Limiter adds a hyperparameter (gamma); requires resampling interval T tuning; APOLLO-Mini with rank-1 needs explicit gradient scale factor (sqrt(128)); theoretical bounds assume fixed projection matrix within T steps; not yet evaluated beyond data-parallel training.
